I traced this by reading the code and grepping. I changed no files. I lost Bash access partway through, so the last two steps used Grep and Read only. The pipeline-level list is the part I checked least.

`CircuitStateController<T>.EnsureNotDisposed` is private, so only methods in `CircuitStateController.cs` call it directly. I left out the legacy `src/Polly/CircuitBreaker/CircuitStateController<TResult>`. It's a different class and doesn't call this method.

## Direct callers (depth 1)
- `CircuitStateController.CircuitState` (getter)
- `CircuitStateController.LastException` (getter)
- `CircuitStateController.LastHandledOutcome` (getter)
- `CircuitStateController.IsolateCircuitAsync`
- `CircuitStateController.CloseCircuitAsync`
- `CircuitStateController.OnActionPreExecuteAsync`
- `CircuitStateController.OnUnhandledOutcomeAsync`
- `CircuitStateController.OnHandledOutcomeAsync`

## Indirect callers
- `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore` calls `OnActionPreExecuteAsync`, `OnHandledOutcomeAsync` and `OnUnhandledOutcomeAsync`.
- `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy..ctor` reaches `CircuitState`, `IsolateCircuitAsync` and `CloseCircuitAsync` only through delegates.
  - It passes `() => _controller.CircuitState` to `CircuitBreakerStateProvider.Initialize`.
  - It passes the isolate and close methods to `CircuitBreakerManualControl.Initialize`.
- `CircuitBreakerStateProvider.CircuitState` (public getter) invokes that stored delegate, so it reaches `CircuitState`.
- `CircuitBreakerManualControl.IsolateAsync` and `CircuitBreakerManualControl.CloseAsync` invoke the registered delegates, so they reach `IsolateCircuitAsync` and `CloseCircuitAsync`.
- `CircuitBreakerManualControl.Initialize` calls `onIsolate` immediately when the control was created isolated. It can therefore reach `IsolateCircuitAsync` during strategy construction.

## Callers of `ExecuteCore`
These reach the controller through `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore`.
- Component layer, which forwards `ExecuteCore` calls: `BridgeComponent.ExecuteCore`, `CompositeComponent.ExecuteCore` (plus `ExecuteCoreWithoutTelemetry` and `ExecuteCoreWithTelemetry`), `DelegatingComponent.ExecuteCore`, `ExecutionTrackingComponent.ExecuteCore`, `ComponentWithDisposeCallbacks.ExecuteCore`, `ReloadableComponent.ExecuteCore`, `ExternalComponent.ExecuteCore` and `PipelineComponent.ExecuteCoreSync`.
- Non-generic `ResiliencePipeline`:
  - `ResiliencePipeline.ExecuteAsync`, all four overloads in `ResiliencePipeline.Async.cs`.
  - `ResiliencePipeline.Execute`, all six overloads in `ResiliencePipeline.Sync.cs`.
- `ResiliencePipeline<T>`:
  - `ResiliencePipeline<T>.ExecuteOutcomeAsync` and `ResiliencePipeline<T>.ExecuteAsync`, all four overloads in `ResiliencePipeline.AsyncT.cs`.
  - `ResiliencePipeline<T>.Execute`, all six overloads in `ResiliencePipeline.SyncT.cs`.
- Other strategies that wrap the next component and so call down into it: `RetryResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore`, `FallbackResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore`, `HedgingResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore`, `TimeoutResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore`, `RateLimiterResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore` and the Chaos strategies' `ExecuteCore`. They reach the circuit breaker only when it sits inside the same pipeline.
- Public registries, extensions and `Polly.Testing` helpers that run or build pipelines (for example `ResiliencePipelineRegistry` and the `Polly.Extensions` DI wiring) can reach it too. I did not enumerate those.

## Tests that exercise it
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/Controller/CircuitStateControllerTests.cs`
  - This is the only file that directly tests the disposed-controller path.
  - Lines 160–170 call `Dispose()` and assert `ObjectDisposedException` from all eight direct callers.
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerResiliencePipelineBuilderTests.cs`
  - Line 230 expects `ObjectDisposedException` from a disposed strategy run through `Execute`.
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategyTests.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerManualControlTests.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerStateProviderTests.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/Issues/IssuesTests.CircuitBreakerStateRegistry_1828.cs`
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/Issues/IssuesTests.CircuitBreakerStateSharing_959.cs`
- `test/Polly.Testing.Tests/ResiliencePipelineExtensionsTests.cs`
- `test/Polly.Extensions.Tests/Issues/IssuesTests.OnCircuitBreakWithServiceProvider_796.cs`
- `test/Polly.Extensions.Tests/Issues/IssuesTests.StrategiesPerEndpoint_1365.cs`

The files after the first two run the circuit breaker through the methods above, so they execute the check. They don't test for the disposed case.
